saturday.notes: Long run, Zone 1 — ~2h on feet. Conversational. Fuel every 30-40 min.

sunday.notes: Easy Zone 1 on tired legs.

monday.notes: Full rest. Cutback week — reduce ~20%. You mentioned August travel; this lighter week is well-timed for it. Keep runs consistent but flexible on which days.

tuesday.notes: Zone 1 easy — travel-friendly, run wherever you are.

wednesday.notes: Tempo: warm up, then 18-20 min at comfortably hard LT2 effort (RPE 7), cool down. If travel makes a tempo impractical, swap with an easy day.

saturday.notes: Reduced long run, Zone 1, easy. Recovery week — keep effort relaxed even if scenery is new.

sunday.notes: Easy Zone 1 jog.

monday.notes: Full rest.

saturday.notes: Long run, Zone 1 — ~2h15. Conversational. Solid fueling practice; treat it like a dress rehearsal for race nutrition.

sunday.notes: Easy Zone 1 on tired legs.

wednesday.notes: Tempo: warm up, then 20 min at comfortably hard LT2 effort (RPE 7), cool down. Maintain sharpness on a lighter week.

saturday.notes: Long run, Zone 1, easy. Slightly reduced — recovery week to set up the peak.

sunday.notes: Easy Zone 1 recovery.

monday.notes: Full rest. PEAK week — highest volume, with back-to-back long runs. This is your biggest training stimulus before the taper.

wednesday.notes: Race-specific tempo: warm up, then 25 min at comfortably hard LT2 effort (RPE 7), cool down. Last hard quality session of the cycle.

thursday.notes: Easy Zone 1 — keep legs loose ahead of the big weekend.

friday.notes: Rest. Prep fuel, hydration, and gear for tomorrow's long run.

saturday.notes: Peak long run, Zone 1 — ~3h on feet. Conversational pace. Full race-day nutrition rehearsal. This is your longest run of the cycle (~50-55% of 50K race distance).

sunday.notes: Back-to-back: medium-long run on tired legs, Zone 1 easy. Simulates the back half of your ultra. Practice power-hiking any rises; keep effort gentle.

monday.notes: Full rest. TAPER begins — volume drops to ~70% of peak, but intensity stays. Do not go all-easy: detraining starts around day 10.

wednesday.notes: Sharpener: warm up, then 15 min at LT2 comfortably hard effort (RPE 7), cool down. Keeps the system primed while volume falls.

saturday.notes: Last longer run of the cycle, Zone 1 easy. Nothing over ~14-16mi from here on. Conversational, relaxed.

sunday.notes: Easy Zone 1 recovery.

monday.notes: Full rest. Taper continues — ~50% of peak volume. Legs should start feeling springy.

wednesday.notes: Maintain intensity: warm up, then 4 x 3 min at LT2 comfortably hard effort (RPE 7) with 2 min easy jog between, cool down. Short and snappy — keeps you sharp without fatigue.

saturday.notes: Final longer run, Zone 1 easy. Stay conversational. Trust the fitness — resist the urge to test yourself.

sunday.notes: Full rest. Begin focusing on sleep, hydration, and carbohydrate stores for race week.

monday.notes: Full rest. RACE WEEK — ~30% of peak volume. Everything now is about arriving fresh.

tuesday.notes: Zone 1 easy, relaxed and short. Legs should feel eager — that's the taper working.

wednesday.notes: Easy Zone 1 with 4 x 20s strides at the end (smooth, controlled, not all-out) to keep neuromuscular sharpness.

thursday.notes: Very short, very easy Zone 1 shakeout. Stay loose; keep it brief.

friday.notes: Complete rest the day before the race. Lay out gear, finalize fueling plan, hydrate, eat well, sleep early.

saturday.notes: RACE DAY (50K). Start in Zone 1 — go out easy and conservative; the discipline you built in training pays off now. Fuel every 30-40 min from the start, power-hike the steep/long climbs by design, and stay relaxed. Negative-split mindset.

sunday.notes: Full rest. Congratulations — begin recovery. Take at least one easy week before resuming normal training.
